newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan raises offshore oil reserves estimate.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan raises offshore oil reserves estimate.

text.p: Turkmenistan has raised its estimate of oil reserves in its 70,000-square kilometre section of the Caspian Sea to 2.8-3.1 billion tonnes from 2.5 billion, Deputy Oil and Gas Minister Khoshgeldy Babaev said on Thursday.

"According to estimates from Turkmenistan and from experts, the territory holds 2.8 to 3.1 billion tonnes of oil," he said in a speech to the Turkmenistan International Oil and Gas 1997 Projects Conference.
He said offshore gas condensate reserves were estimated at 690 million tonnes.

Turkmenistan is preparing a tender for exploration and production rights to about half a dozen offshore blocks, which officials said had attracted interest from major international oil and gas companies.

But officials from two potential international investors said huge exploitable oil finds -- such as those being developed by an $8 billion multinational consortium in the Azeri sector of the Caspian -- were unlikely in the Turkmen area to be tendered.
The government views the success of the sale as crucial in attracting much-needed foreign investment to its huge untapped energy sector.
"Documents are now being drafted to hold a tender to prospect and produce oil and gas in the Caspian," Babaev said, adding, "The tender will be held this year."
But uncertainty surrounds the timing of the sale, because Turkmenistan has said it will not go ahead until differences over territorial claims with other countries bordering the Caspian are settled.
The tender was originally scheduled for early 1997.
